title: Things to Do in Hyderabad: Charminar, Golconda, Palaces, Biryani & More
seoTitle: Things to Do in Hyderabad: Heritage & Food | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Hyderabad: the Charminar and Laad Bazaar, Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace, the Salar Jung Museum, Golconda Fort and its light show, the Qutb Shahi tombs, Hussain Sagar, Birla Mandir, Ramoji Film City, the Statue of Equality, biryani, haleem and Irani chai.
dek: The city of the Qutb Shahis and the Nizams, where a 16th-century monument, royal palaces and one of India's greatest museums meet a booming tech city and a legendary food culture.
secondaryKeywords: things to do in Hyderabad at night
searchIntent: First-time visitors, families and business travellers planning two to three days in Hyderabad.
intro: Hyderabad was founded in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, fifth ruler of the Qutb Shahi dynasty, who moved his capital from the fortress of Golconda. From the 18th century until 1948, it was ruled by the Nizams, among the richest rulers in the world. Today it is the capital of Telangana and one of India's biggest technology hubs.

The things to do in Hyderabad span four centuries: the Charminar and the bazaars and mosques of the old city, the Nizams' Chowmahalla Palace, the vast Salar Jung Museum, the ruined fortress of Golconda and the domed Qutb Shahi tombs, and the lake of Hussain Sagar. Newer attractions include Ramoji Film City and the Statue of Equality. And there is the food: biryani, haleem, Irani chai and Osmania biscuits.
Two to three days covers the city. October to February is the most comfortable time.
quickAnswer: See the Charminar and shop in Laad Bazaar
Climb Golconda Fort and watch its light show
Take a boat to the Buddha statue on Hussain Sagar
Spend a day at Ramoji Film City
Eat biryani, haleem and Irani chai

items.name: See the Charminar

image.alt: Charminar with street life around it
image.caption: Charminar

body: The Charminar, built in 1591, is a square monument with four minarets about 56 metres high, standing at the heart of the old city. Visitors can climb to the first floor for views of the bazaars. It is lit up in the evening, and the area is busiest and most atmospheric during Ramzan nights.

items.name: Shop in Laad Bazaar
body: Laad Bazaar, leading west from the Charminar, is famous for lacquer bangles studded with stones, along with bridal wear, perfumes (attar) and pearls. Hyderabad has long been known as the city of pearls; buy from reputed shops.

items.name: Visit Mecca Masjid
body: Mecca Masjid, near the Charminar, is one of the largest mosques in India, begun in the 1610s. Bricks made with soil brought from Mecca are said to be set above the central arch. Visitors should dress modestly and avoid prayer times.

items.name: Tour Chowmahalla Palace
body: Chowmahalla Palace, the seat of the Asaf Jahi Nizams, has four palaces around courtyards, a grand Durbar Hall with crystal chandeliers, and collections of vintage cars, clothes and arms. It is closed on Fridays.

items.name: Explore the Salar Jung Museum
body: The Salar Jung Museum holds one of the world's largest collections assembled by a single person, Salar Jung III, including the Veiled Rebecca marble sculpture, a musical clock that draws crowds at every hour, Mughal miniatures, jade, textiles and European art. It is closed on Fridays.

items.name: Climb Golconda Fort
body: Golconda Fort, west of the city, was the capital of the Qutb Shahi kingdom and a centre of the diamond trade; the Koh-i-Noor is believed to have come from mines in the region. A clap at the Fateh Darwaza gate can be heard at the top of the hill, an early acoustic warning system. The climb to the Baradari at the top takes about 30 to 45 minutes.

items.name: Watch the light and sound show

image.alt: Sound and light show at Golconda Fort
image.caption: Golconda light show

body: The evening sound and light show at Golconda narrates the fort's history, with shows in English, Hindi and Telugu on different days.

items.name: See the Qutb Shahi tombs
body: The Qutb Shahi tombs, a short drive from Golconda, are a group of domed tombs of the dynasty's rulers and their families, set in gardens. A long restoration has brought the complex back to life, with a heritage park and stepwells.

items.name: Take a boat to the Buddha statue
body: Hussain Sagar, a lake built in 1562, has a large monolithic Buddha statue on a rock in the middle, reached by boat from Lumbini Park or Eat Street. Necklace Road around the lake is lively in the evening, and a laser show is held at Lumbini Park.

items.name: Visit Birla Mandir
body: Birla Mandir, a white marble temple to Venkateswara on Naubat Pahad, has views over Hussain Sagar, especially at sunset. Phones and cameras are not allowed inside.

items.name: Spend a day at Ramoji Film City

image.alt: Film sets at Ramoji Film City
image.caption: Ramoji Film City

body: Ramoji Film City, about 30 km from the city, is one of the world's largest film studio complexes, with film sets, shows, rides and gardens. It is a full-day outing popular with families.

items.name: See the Statue of Equality
body: The Statue of Equality at Muchintal, unveiled in 2022, is a 216-foot seated statue of the 11th-century philosopher Ramanuja, with a complex of 108 shrines and a musical fountain show.

items.name: Visit Chilkur Balaji
body: The Chilkur Balaji Temple, on the city's edge, is popularly known as the visa temple, as many devotees pray here for successful visa applications.

items.name: See the Paigah Tombs
body: The Paigah Tombs, the burial ground of a noble family closely linked to the Nizams, have remarkable marble lattice screens, stucco work and inlaid decoration. They are rarely crowded.

items.name: Visit Falaknuma Palace
body: Falaknuma Palace, built in the 1890s on a hilltop and later owned by the Nizams, is now a luxury hotel. Access is generally for guests and for dining or heritage experiences booked in advance.

items.name: See Taramati Baradari and Shilparamam
body: Taramati Baradari, a Qutb Shahi pavilion near Golconda, hosts cultural events. Shilparamam, a crafts village in Madhapur, has stalls of handicrafts from across India and folk performances.

items.name: Walk around Durgam Cheruvu
body: Durgam Cheruvu, a lake in the tech district, has a cable-stayed bridge that is lit up at night and a lakeside walkway, a favourite modern evening spot.

items.name: Eat Hyderabadi biryani and haleem
body: Hyderabadi biryani, made in the kachchi (raw marinated meat) style, is the city's pride. During Ramzan, haleem, a slow-cooked wheat and meat dish with a GI tag, is sold from evening stalls. Try double ka meetha and qubani ka meetha for dessert.

items.name: Drink Irani chai with Osmania biscuits
body: The city's Irani cafés serve sweet, milky chai with Osmania biscuits and bun maska. Some near the Charminar have been open for generations.

items.name: Celebrate Bathukamma or Numaish
body: Bathukamma, a floral festival of Telangana in September or October, fills the city with flower towers and dancing women. The Numaish, an annual industrial exhibition and fair, runs from January to February.

items.name: October to February
body: Pleasant weather for the old city, Golconda and the lakes. The Deccan Festival and Numaish exhibition bring events and food fairs.

items.name: March to June
body: Very hot days; plan indoor museums at midday and forts in the late afternoon. Ramzan, when it falls in these months, brings night food markets around the Charminar.

items.name: July to September
body: Monsoon showers cool the city; Bathukamma and Bonalu festivals add colour.

oneDay: Start at the Charminar and Mecca Masjid, walk through Laad Bazaar, and visit Chowmahalla Palace. After a biryani lunch, spend the afternoon at Golconda Fort and stay for the light and sound show.
tips: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport is about 30 km from the centre.
Several museums and palaces close on Fridays; plan around them.
Use the metro and app cabs to avoid traffic.
Summers are very hot; see Golconda in the late afternoon.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Hyderabad?
faqs.a: See the Charminar and Laad Bazaar, Mecca Masjid, Chowmahalla Palace, the Salar Jung Museum, Golconda Fort and the Qutb Shahi tombs, take a boat on Hussain Sagar, visit Ramoji Film City and eat biryani.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Hyderabad at night?
faqs.a: The Golconda light and sound show, Necklace Road and the Hussain Sagar laser show, Birla Mandir at dusk and, in Ramzan, the food stalls around the Charminar.
